sub_scenario.family: negotiating scope commitments when project evidence is incomplete
sub_scenario.one_line: housing programme officer: fund investigation before any build pledge

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the repair queue and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The resident file review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can approve a standard accessibility repair when the assessment and landlord consent are on file.
Are urgent requests normally hard to handle?
No, clear evidence lets me move quickly.
Someone new shadowed me in the programme office this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the allocation rounds into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
The courtyard access request contains residents' concerns and a rough drawing, but no survey of drainage, ownership boundary, or affected households.
What would a full commitment overlook?
Whether the proposed path is permitted, buildable, and useful to those expected to use it.
I helped arrange a temporary ramp last winter after an occupational assessment described its dimensions.
What made that possible?
The need, location, and permitted work were specific.
I archived last cycle's notes on the resident file and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
There is a small resident-engagement budget available before the next allocation round.
Can that finance construction?
No, it can fund a survey and structured feedback sessions.
A vendor call about the repair queue ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the programme office checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the allocation rounds.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the resident file records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
At the tenant meeting, the residents association agreed to gather affected-household responses and allow a surveyor to inspect the courtyard before any design is selected.
What can you offer now?
A survey-and-engagement package, not a promise to build the sketched path.
I sketched next week's plan for the allocation rounds before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the repair queue updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The allocation panel meets in eight weeks.
Does that require a construction pledge today?
No, it gives time to bring verified options to the panel.
A local newsletter has offered to feature a pledge for a new accessible courtyard.
Does publicity answer the drainage or ownership questions?
No, it would make a promise ahead of the needed evidence.
I closed the week by updating the programme office handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Should I promise to build the courtyard path described in the request?
